title.narrative: Integrated Health and WASH Cholera Emergency Response in Sharg El-Nile, Kariri, Um Bada, and Omdurman, Khartoum State

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International (RI) and its partner APD aimed to address the health and WASH needs of individuals in Sharg El Nile, Kariri, Um Bada, and Omdurman, localities in Khartoum state. The project sought to reach individuals by improving access to healthcare and WASH services and mainstreaming protection and nutrition services. The project strengthened primary healthcare services and cholera response, including emergency trauma response and outbreak management, and strengthened referral mechanisms in collaboration with the State Ministry of Health (SMoH), addressing diseases such as measles, malaria, and cholera. Integrated Community Case Management (iCCM) was implemented by APD to ensure early diagnosis and treatment of common diseases at the community level and received support to ensure continuity of care. ltbrgtThrough this project, RI and its partners are planning to reach 51,238 (17,173 W 12,230 G 11,750M 11,750 B) beneficiaries through health interventions and 46,450 Individuals (12,319 G, 11,836 B, 11,371 W, 10,925 M) with WASH services and 9,407 Individuals (3,821 G, 3,321 B, 1,744 W, 453 M) through nutrition services. Additionally, protection and nutrition activities were designed to address the comprehensive needs of vulnerable populations, particularly women and girls. RI enhanced healthcare by providing staff incentives, ensuring the availability of medical supplies (in coordination with WHO and UNICEF), and procuring buffer stock, drugs, and equipment. Staff received capacity building support. ltbrgtRI provided integrated primary healthcare services at ten health facilities: Alsabail, Almarkhyat, Alfetimab, Alsalam 1, and Alsalam 12 in Umbada locality Abosnigedc in Kariri locality Al Samra and Suba Sharge in Sharg El Nile locality, Wad el Amine and elTekinab PHCs in Sharge Nil locality delivering comprehensive reproductive healthcare as well as OPD consultations for the management of communicable diseases, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support Services (MHPSS), cholera response, and health awareness activities. Health services were integrated with WASH interventions, with protection and nutrition mainstreamed across all components. At the community level, APD implemented iCCM services, with Community Health Workers (CHWs) linked to each facility for supply replenishment and patient referrals. ltbrgtIn WASH ltbrgtRI implemented integrated WASH interventions with a focus on cholera response and support to displacement affected communities. Key activities included the provision of safe water through trucking, rehabilitation of water sources, water quality monitoring, and chlorination efforts, including targeted supply to Cholera Treatment Units and Centers (CTUs/CTCs). ltbrgtHygiene promotion was prioritized through the distribution of WASH kits, hygiene support for CTUs/CTCs, and deployment of CATI/CORT teams to strengthen community level cholera prevention and hygiene behavior change. Sanitation support included the rehabilitation of facilities, waste management, and environmental cleaning to reduce public health risks. ltbrgtAll interventions were closely coordinated with the State Ministry of Health (SMoH), local authorities, and community structures to ensure efficiency, alignment, and accountability. The project applied a conflict sensitive “do no harm” approach, with protection principles and community engagement mainstreamed throughout implementation. Monitoring, evaluation, and feedback systems guided responsive and adaptive service delivery. ltbrgtMonitoring visits were conducted by the State Ministry of Health (SMoH), and Relief International (RI) staff tracked patient treatment progress and provided on the job coaching to enhance the quality of care. Protection interventions were mainstreamed with a targeted focus on vulnerable populations, particularly women and girls. The project applied a conflict sensitive approach rooted in the "do no harm" principle. ltbrgt ltbrgtlt/pgt
